data.title: Suspicious "final reminder before seizure" from EuroClaim (Cyprus)
data.summary: EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd. (Cyprus) demands €287.40 by 6 August 2026 for an alleged phone-signed prize-draw subscription, threatening account seizure, a SCHUFA entry and criminal charges. The letter shows many scam indicators.
data.explanation: This letter demands €287.40 within 72 hours for a "Lotto-Muster-Club" subscription supposedly concluded by phone. It has hallmarks of a scam or an abusive collection letter: a generic salutation, a 72-hour deadline, threats of seizure and criminal charges, and payment to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private person. An account seizure needs a court order first. Do not pay under pressure. Check whether you ever had this subscription. A consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) can help, and you can report the letter to the police if it is a scam. Keep the letter. The letter's claim that an objection is pointless is not a legal fact.

warnings: Payment is demanded to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private person, not a company account.
A 72-hour deadline and threats of seizure, SCHUFA entry and criminal charges without notice are typical pressure tactics.
Generic salutation 'Sehr geehrte/r Schuldner/in' and no contract details or itemised basis for the claim.
The added fees of €84.00 and €24.00 look inflated and unexplained.
The claim that an objection is pointless should not be relied on.
